charts.title: Small native allocations can learn pointer following
charts.takeaway: Two native channels plus attention reach 96.1%; the six-channel dip shows that wider is not always better.
charts.note: Saved rounded table aggregates; bars show sample SD, not confidence intervals. Common LR and unequal budgets; not tuned-method superiority.

charts.title: A smaller update is not automatically faster or less disruptive
charts.takeaway: Most fits take roughly 50 recorded RL minutes; retention and task accuracy are separate measurements.
charts.note: Table aggregates. RL clocks exclude evaluation and are not FLOPs. The later tuned rank-one LoRA pointer result is 99.7%, under a different recipe.

charts.title: Two-task training has strong native and LoRA solutions
charts.takeaway: Native routing + preservation works well; LoRA preservation without reward routing is equally strong here.
charts.note: Rounded means across 3 seeds; per-cell seed uncertainty is not displayed. Native 117 channels versus LoRA rank 18; not an attention ablation.

charts.title: Separately learned skills interfere when enabled together
charts.takeaway: Strong standalone specialists lose about 21–29 percentage points when all eight updates are active.
charts.note: Means and sample SD from saved aggregate tables. Two updates average all pairs; four average eight balanced subsets. No oracle task selection.

charts.title: Arithmetic and pointer following show especially large combination losses
charts.takeaway: The macro score hides strong skill suppression and weakly learned tasks; Sudoku remains difficult even alone.
charts.note: Rounded three-seed means, without cellwise error bars. These are separate task prompts, not chained multi-skill solutions.

charts.title: A fair comparison includes development-only mixture calibration
charts.takeaway: Calibrated small-budget LoRA exceeds native; medium budgets nearly tie. Retention ordering also changes.
charts.note: Accuracy bars show sample SD. Perplexity bars are rounded aggregate means without uncertainty in the saved table. Some calibrated coefficients are zero.

charts.title: Benchmark effects are mixed, rather than uniform information loss
charts.takeaway: MMLU declines in every displayed condition; ARC-Easy usually improves. Calibration changes these trade-offs too.
charts.note: Saved rounded aggregate means, without benchmark-wise uncertainty. This fixed, repeatedly inspected panel is descriptive and cannot establish general knowledge retention.

charts.title: Combining updates is different from executing skills in a pipeline
charts.takeaway: Pointer → arithmetic benefits greatly from explicit orchestration; stack → sorting does not show the same gain.
charts.note: Rounded means. Direct and pipeline conditions use different prompts/execution; this is not a controlled estimate of one-pass compositional ability.

charts.title: Joint continuation improves coexistence; conservation reduces text drift
charts.takeaway: Training in the shared model already helps. The extra losses motivated the later component ablations.
charts.note: Saved rounded means and sample SD. This first continuation study is separate from the later 48-bank factorial; results are not pooled.

charts.title: Preservation and conservation address different outcomes
charts.takeaway: Preservation improves combined skills; conservation gives the largest reduction in measured text drift.
charts.note: Means ± sample SD. All arms retain joint-aware RL/reference KL. The follow-up reuses 24 archived controls once, rather than adding replications.

charts.title: The complete factorial separates coexistence gains from text retention
charts.takeaway: Foreign preservation usually helps combined skills; conservation sharply lowers perplexity drift across preservation settings.
charts.note: Means ± sample SD. Width 4 native versus rank 1 LoRA. All conditions retain joint-aware RL/reference KL; this is not a native-versus-LoRA superiority test.

charts.title: Reduced text drift does not establish broad accuracy gains
charts.takeaway: Multiple-choice changes remain small and mixed; these measurements qualify what the conservation objective establishes.
charts.note: Means ± sample SD across three seeds. Negative = lower accuracy than base. Absolute accuracy is not shown. Repeatedly inspected benchmarks, not a fresh confirmatory test.

charts.title: The foreign-preservation advantage is clearer than the self advantage
charts.takeaway: Foreign beats self in 11 of 12 paired comparisons; those comparisons share three seeds and are not 12 independent replications.
charts.note: Individual seeds and their mean; no population confidence intervals. Positive values match the predicted term in each panel; axes differ.

charts.title: Pointer following drives much of the preservation gain
charts.takeaway: Blue cells improve with foreign preservation; red cells regress. Better macro accuracy does not mean every skill is protected.
charts.note: Paired three-seed means from saved analysis. This plot is a component contrast, not change relative to the pretrained base.

charts.title: The initial Colab pilot learned the original wording, with weak transfer
charts.takeaway: Primary refusal was strong; alternate wording failed badly for routed and scattered updates in this pilot.
charts.note: Actual saved Colab measurements, not the initial failed arithmetic task. Routed/scattered train 200,704 scalars; the server's single-layer study uses 10,752.

charts.title: The Colab pilot tracked refusal and answer recovery throughout removal
charts.takeaway: Routed and scattered starts recover primary answers after one observed update; the full-model start takes two here.
charts.note: One-seed pilot. X axis is linear through update 4 and logarithmic thereafter. Dots are actual observations; joining lines do not imply measured intermediate points.

charts.title: Localized refusal can be acquired, then rapidly removed
charts.takeaway: Eight of nine localized starts qualify; every qualified localized model recovers answers within 1–2 updates.
charts.note: Dots are individual seeds. Acquisition budgets/rates differ: 10,752 native scalars versus 494M full-model parameters. Later thresholds are interval-censored by evaluation spacing.

charts.title: Full-model removal can behave differently from simple refusal disappearance
charts.takeaway: Refusal can disappear, return, or give way to wrong answers; report answer correctness alongside refusal.
charts.note: Step 0 is after refusal acquisition. The original base answered these copying prompts. Localized groups n=3/2/3; full-model n=3. Curves use saved evaluations only.

charts.title: Exploratory bypass: protecting a region does not protect its behaviour
charts.takeaway: This was a mechanism exploration; the next graph uses matched two-block update budgets.
charts.note: Means and observed seed ranges. Early/late n=3; middle n=2 qualified acquisitions. Unrestricted reference has a different parameter budget. Original prompt forms.

charts.title: Other blocks can override refusal while the acquisition block stays frozen
charts.takeaway: Late-layer low-rate refusal survives eight updates; every high-rate adjacent-block run reaches zero within four.
charts.note: Means and observed seed ranges. Early/late n=3; middle n=2 qualified acquisitions. Unrestricted reference has a different parameter budget. Original prompt forms.

charts.title: Refusal rate alone can mischaracterize a removal trajectory
charts.takeaway: One model loses refusal on alternate wording first; others stop refusing but still produce wrong answers.
charts.note: Alternate wording was excluded from SFT but used in acquisition validation; it is not untouched OOD. Right: layer 22, after-block mask, LR 1e-5, update 8.

charts.title: The late-layer plateau is a delay, not lasting protection
charts.takeaway: All six runs eventually reach zero refusal, first at updates 13–37; answer recovery can occur at a different time.
charts.note: Each curve is an individual trajectory. Dotted line marks the original eight-update window. Frozen acquisition block verified; these are extensions, not fresh seeds.

charts.title: Capability damage depends on the task and removal protocol
charts.takeaway: Arithmetic drops in 5/6 extended runs, averaging −10.9 pp; other protocols show mixed losses and gains.
charts.note: 32 items per diagnostic task; one changed answer = 3.125 pp. Trajectories reuse acquisition seeds. Green copying remains 100% at the recorded endpoints.

charts.title: Spreading the same small refusal budget did not give durable protection
charts.takeaway: Every qualified trajectory first reaches zero refusal and ≥90% correct answering within one or two updates.
charts.note: Removal was measured through update 64; chart zooms to 0–8. Lines are means with observed seed ranges; group n=2/3/2. Acquisition failures are retained on the left.

charts.title: COSMIC: implementation exists, but no completed outcome is available here
charts.takeaway: There is no numerical COSMIC result to graph in this checkout; the absence of a local export does not prove it never ran.
charts.note: The earlier A/B direction pilot in Downloads is a different experiment and is not substituted for the authors' COSMIC procedure.
